disease_label_per_paper: Perinephric abscess causing mycotic celiac and splenic artery aneurysm
presentation_summary: 57-year-old woman presented to the emergency room with one week of left-sided flank pain, flank swelling, poor appetite, and subjective fever.
History included a remote left kidney infection five years earlier requiring antibiotics and percutaneous drainage.
Initial vitals were blood pressure 116/65 mmHg, heart rate 101/min, and temperature 99.1 F; exam showed soft tender left-flank swelling without crepitus or erythema.
Urinalysis showed pyuria with 477 WBC/HPF; serum labs showed WBC 15,400/uL and creatinine 3.4 mg/dL.

Non-contrast CT abdomen/pelvis showed emphysematous pyelonephritis, multiple left ureteral and renal pelvic stones, and a 13.3 x 9.4 x 18 cm left retroperitoneal/perinephric abscess extending into pelvis, paraspinal musculature, psoas muscle, and left-flank fat plane.

microbiology.result: Pan-sensitive Escherichia coli and Streptococcus anginosus

procedures.source_text_value: Two emergent CT-guided percutaneous tubes were placed and 250 ml purulent fluid was drained
During the first operative phase, 1200 mL purulent fluid was evacuated
On hospital day 11 the patient was taken back to the operating room for definitive nephrectomy

clinical_course.event: Started parenteral vancomycin and imipenem with CT-guided drainage; later narrowed to ceftriaxone and metronidazole after cultures.
Creatinine improved to 1.1 mg/dL after fluids, but leukocytosis rose to 25,000/uL, drain output was minimal, and flank swelling/pain worsened with crepitus.
Repeat CT showed enlarging multiloculated abscess with air-fluid levels and subcutaneous extension; operative drainage evacuated 1200 mL pus.
Definitive nephrectomy attempt found mycotic aneurysms of the aorta, celiac and splenic arteries with massive bleeding; splenic artery bleeding could not be controlled and the patient died.

actual_treatment: ceftriaxone and metronidazole after initial cultures

outcome.source_text_value: splenic artery bleeding could not be controlled and the patient expired on the operating table

quality_warnings: Post-drainage culture results, antibiotic de-escalation, repeat CT worsening, operative findings, and fatal vascular complication are preserved but use_in_ranking=false.
This case has overlap with renal abscess/emphysematous pyelonephritis and nephrolithiasis; perinephric-space collection size and extension are retained rather than narrowing the disease name.
Initial CT did not report vascular invasion; the vascular hazard is therefore present only as post-diagnosis course evidence.
